title: How Much Is One Hour of Your Life Worth? (40 Countries Exposed)
description:
What is one hour of your life worth? The answer depends almost entirely on where you were born.

We compared hourly wages, working hours, and purchasing power across 40 countries using OECD, World Bank, and ILO data — then plotted them all on one chart. Four quadrants emerged: the Dream, the Grind, the Trap, and the Chill. Where your country lands might surprise you.

📊 Key findings:
• Luxembourg earns $64.12/hr — the highest in the dataset
• Germany works the fewest hours (1,340/yr) and still earns $51.82/hr
• The USA works 439 more hours than Denmark per year — for just ~11% more pay
• Mexico: 2,226 hours/yr at $9.18/hr — the OECD extreme
• Cambodia: $2.30/hr, 2,389 hours — Germany earns 22.5× more per hour while working 1,049 fewer hours
